form_011:n1.prompt:
You are helping me choose a formation service for setting up my LLC. I am forming an LLC (not a Delaware C-Corp) as the default structure for a holding company, agency, or bootstrapped business.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear: my target state of formation, whether I need a registered agent included, my rough budget, and whether I have a preference for a fully online service versus a local attorney.

Then research and compare at least three real formation options that fit my situation — for example Stripe Atlas, LegalZoom, Northwest Registered Agent, ZenBusiness, or a local business attorney. For each, gather from their official websites: total cost (including state filing fees and registered agent fees), turnaround time, what's included (name check, Articles of Organization filing, registered agent service, operating agreement template, EIN filing assistance, banking setup help, state tax registration support), renewal/ongoing fees, and any notable limitations or customer support differences.

Organize this into a clear side-by-side comparison table with pros and cons for each option relevant to my stated priorities (cost, speed, state coverage, support quality, add-on services).

Do not select or purchase a service on my behalf — this decision is subjective and depends on my specific tradeoffs, so it remains a human step. Present the comparison and your observations, then stop for human sign-off so I can review and make the final choice myself.

Report back with: the comparison table, a short summary of key differences, and any open questions you need me to answer (e.g., state of formation) before you can complete the research.

form_011:n2.prompt:
You are helping me check LLC name availability for the state where I'm forming my LLC (I'll default to Delaware unless I tell you otherwise). Before starting, ask me for: (1) the formation state if not Delaware, (2) my top 3-5 candidate LLC names in priority order (including the required 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company' suffix variant I prefer), and (3) my business domain/website if I have one, so you can cross-check name-related branding consistency.

Once you have the names, use the state's official entity name search tool (for Delaware, the Division of Corporations' entity search site) to check each candidate in priority order. For each name, record: whether it appears available or already taken/reserved, the exact match or near-match results shown, and any obvious conflicts (identical or confusingly similar existing entities). If the state site requires solving a captcha or blocks automated access, note that and describe the manual steps I'd need to take instead.

Also flag any names that are likely to be rejected for containing restricted words (e.g., 'Bank,' 'Insurance,' 'University') based on common state naming rules, even if the search tool doesn't explicitly flag them.

When done, report back: a table of each candidate name, its availability status, any conflicting entities found, and your recommended top choice plus a backup, given availability and how well each preserves my intended branding. Do not attempt to reserve or file the name — that remains a human step requiring direct action on the state's site. Just give me the availability findings and recommendation so I can proceed to reservation or filing myself.

form_011:n3.prompt:
You are helping me file Articles of Organization for my new LLC and appoint a registered agent using {{vendor}}, a legal-ops formation platform. This is a state-recorded legal filing requiring my personal attestation, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off — do not submit, sign, or approve anything on my behalf.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already known: my LLC's desired name (plus 1-2 backup names), the state of formation, my business address, the names/addresses of all members or managers, my business purpose (brief description), and whether I already have an account with {{vendor}}.

Then do the following:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials (or note that I need to create an account if none exists).
2. Run a name availability check for my desired LLC name and backups in the chosen state; report which names are available.
3. Confirm whether I want {{vendor}} to serve as my registered agent (noting it offers digital scanned mail and service-of-process handling) or whether I'll designate another agent.
4. Fill in the Articles of Organization form fields (entity name, state, registered agent, address, member/manager info, purpose) as a draft — do not submit.
5. Note the filing fee and any state processing time estimates.
6. Compile a checklist summarizing: chosen name, registered agent selection, all draft field values, fee amount, and the exact submit button/step where my attestation is required.

When done, report back with: the availability results, the completed draft summary, the registered agent choice, fee/timeline info, and a clear statement that the filing is staged and ready but requires my review and explicit approval to submit, since I must personally attest to the formation details under state law.

form_011:n4.prompt:
You are helping me track the pending arrival of my LLC's stamped Certificate of Formation from the state's Secretary of State (or equivalent) filings office. This document cannot be produced or retrieved by you — the state office processes and issues it on its own timeline, and there is no interface for you to check its status, so receiving it remains a human step.

Please prepare the tracking and follow-up materials so I'm organized while I wait. Ask me for: (1) which state I filed in, (2) the filing date and any confirmation/receipt number I received, (3) the registered agent's name and contact method (since the Certificate is often delivered to them by mail or email), and (4) the state's stated typical processing time if I know it.

Using that information, produce: a short status-tracking checklist noting the expected delivery window and where I should check for updates (e.g., the state filing office's public status-lookup page, if one exists, or my registered agent's portal/email — note I will need to check these myself); a reminder note with a suggested date to follow up if nothing has arrived by the end of the typical processing window; and a simple checklist of next actions to take once the Certificate arrives (e.g., save a copy, proceed to EIN application, operating agreement signing, bank account opening).

Do not attempt to contact the state office, submit any forms, or check any status page yourself — this waiting and monitoring remains a human step for me to complete. Report back with the prepared checklist and reminder note, and stop for human sign-off before I take any further action.

form_011:n5.prompt:
You are helping me draft the operating agreement for my newly formed LLC. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: the LLC's exact legal name, state of formation, registered agent name/address, the LLC's principal business address, whether it is single-member or multi-member (and if multi-member, the names, addresses, and ownership percentages of each member), the management structure (member-managed vs manager-managed), how profits/losses and distributions will be allocated, and any special provisions I want (e.g., transfer restrictions, buy-sell terms, capital contribution rules, dissolution procedures).

Using this information, draft a complete operating agreement covering: company formation details, member roles and ownership percentages, capital contributions, profit/loss allocation, distribution rules, management authority and voting procedures, admission/withdrawal of members, transfer restrictions, dissolution and winding-up procedures, and standard boilerplate (governing law, amendment process, severability). Tailor single-member agreements to be simpler (focused on liability protection and formalities) versus multi-member agreements (focused on governance and conflict prevention).

Produce the draft as a clean, well-organized document with clearly labeled sections and blank signature lines for each member, dated. Do not submit, notarize, or sign the document — signing the operating agreement remains a human step that only the members can complete.

When done, report back: (1) the full draft text or a link to the saved document, (2) a checklist of any missing details you had to leave as placeholders, and (3) a reminder that I and any other members need to review, finalize, and sign the agreement, then store it with the company's official records.

form_011:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the operating agreement for my newly formed LLC so it is ready for member signatures. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: the LLC's legal name and state of formation, the registered agent's name/address, the full list of members with their legal names, emails, ownership percentages, and capital contributions, the intended management structure (member-managed vs. manager-managed), and any special provisions I want included (vesting, buy-sell terms, voting thresholds, distribution rules). Also ask whether I already have a draft operating agreement or want you to prepare one from a standard template.

Once you have these inputs: (1) draft or finalize the operating agreement text, covering ownership percentages, capital contributions, management structure, voting rights, profit/loss distributions, transfer restrictions, and dissolution terms; (2) proofread it for internal consistency (percentages sum to 100%, names/entities match formation documents); (3) prepare a signing workflow using an e-signature service such as DocuSign or HelloSign — set up the envelope/template with each member as a named signer, correct signing order if relevant, and email addresses filled in, but do NOT send it for signature or trigger the signing yet; (4) compile a checklist of any outstanding items (missing member info, unresolved terms).

Do not sign, consent to, or submit the agreement on behalf of any member — this is a policy-gate step. Each member's signature is a personal legal act that only they can perform, so you must stop for human sign-off once the draft and e-sign envelope are prepared.

Report back with: the finalized draft text (or a summary of key terms), the status of the prepared e-sign envelope, the list of members and their signing status, and a clear checklist of what remains before I can circulate it for actual signatures.

form_011:n7.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to apply for an EIN (Employer Identification Number) for my newly formed LLC directly through the IRS. Do not submit anything on my behalf — the IRS requires the LLC's 'responsible party' to personally attest to their identity under penalty of perjury, so the actual submission remains a human step.

First, ask me for any details you need that aren't already known: the LLC's exact legal name as filed in the Articles of Organization, the state and date of formation, the LLC's mailing and physical address, the number of LLC members, the business's principal activity/industry, the reason for applying (e.g., new business), the responsible party's full legal name and title, and whether the responsible party has an SSN or ITIN (do not ask me to share the actual number).

Using this information, prepare a complete draft of the IRS Form SS-4 fields exactly as they'd need to appear in the IRS's online EIN application wizard at https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/get-an-employer-identification-number — organized field-by-field so I can copy them in myself. Also prepare a short checklist covering: what information I'll need to have on hand (including my SSN/ITIN, which you should never ask me to paste), the expected time to complete the online session (it must be finished in one sitting), and confirmation that only the responsible party may submit it.

When the draft and checklist are ready, present them to me clearly and then stop for human sign-off — I will personally log in, enter the attested information, and submit the application myself. Report back with the completed draft SS-4 field list and checklist, and note explicitly that submission is pending my action.

form_011:n8.prompt:
You are helping me open a business bank account for my LLC using {{vendor}}, a startup banking platform. Please prepare everything needed so I can complete and submit the actual application myself, since the bank must perform identity verification (KYC/AML) on me as the authorized signer, which you cannot do.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: my LLC's legal name, EIN, state and date of formation, registered agent details, business address, my role (e.g., sole member/manager), and my personal identification details format the bank requests (do not ask me to share the actual ID numbers or documents with you—just note what's required).

Then:
1. Compile a checklist of documents typically required to open the account (Articles of Organization, EIN confirmation letter, operating agreement, government ID, business address proof) and note which ones I have versus still need.
2. Draft the business information fields (company name, address, EIN, ownership structure, expected use of account) in a form-ready summary I can copy into the {{vendor}} application.
3. Summarize {{vendor}}'s relevant capabilities I should confirm during onboarding: checking application status online, viewing account/routing numbers and generating a bank verification letter anytime, and completing onboarding in about a week.
4. Note that identity verification and signature authority confirmation are required directly from me and cannot be completed by you.

When finished, give me: (a) the completed document checklist, (b) the pre-filled application summary, (c) a short list of next steps for me to personally verify my identity and submit the application, and (d) explicitly state that this remains a human step and stop for human sign-off before any submission or identity verification occurs.

form_011:n9.prompt:
You are helping me register my newly formed LLC for state tax accounts. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the state(s) where my LLC is formed and/or does business, (2) my LLC's legal name and formation date, (3) my EIN (already issued), (4) my registered business address and mailing address, (5) my NAICS/business activity code or a plain description of what the business does, (6) my expected start date for sales/employment activity, and (7) whether I have employees (for unemployment/withholding tax) or sell taxable goods/services (for sales tax).

Once I provide these, go to the official state tax authority website for the state(s) I specify (e.g., the state's Department of Revenue or equivalent) and locate the business tax registration portal. Complete the registration form(s) using the details I gave you — this typically includes registering for a state income/franchise tax account, sales & use tax permit if applicable, and employer withholding/unemployment insurance tax if I have employees. Use my configured credentials to log in if an account is required. Fill in all fields accurately, double-check the EIN and legal name match what's on file with the state, and submit the registration directly since this is a straightforward data-entry form with no signature-of-authority requirement blocking submission.

After submission, capture and report back to me: the confirmation number(s), the resulting state tax account ID(s), which tax types were registered, any expected follow-up mail/email from the state, and estimated processing time. If the portal requires me to create a personal login tied to my SSN or asks for anything beyond standard business registration data, pause and ask me before proceeding. Flag any state-specific quirks (e.g., separate registrations for sales tax vs. withholding) you encounter.
